matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, recompute the integer values of both sides of the equation and verify that the equality holds; without this, the model may output an equation that is still false.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a transformation, always calculate the numeric values of the left and right sides to confirm they match.
matchstick.example: Proposing a new equation without checking that 12 = 13 - 12, which remains false.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting glyph must correspond to a valid Roman numeral; otherwise the character becomes invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick relocation, ensure both the source and destination characters remain recognizable Roman numerals.
matchstick.example: Removing a vertical stick from a solitary I, leaving an empty (non‑numeral) character.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: A stick’s orientation (vertical, horizontal, diagonal) is fixed; you may only relocate it preserving its orientation. Moving a diagonal stick to a vertical slot creates an invalid shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Before moving a stick, check its orientation and ensure the destination character can accept that orientation.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal stick from an X to a minus sign, which expects a horizontal stick.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: A single stick move can affect at most the source character (which loses one stick) and the destination character (which gains one stick); altering more characters violates the one‑stick rule.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When planning a move, restrict modifications to only the two involved characters.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘XIII’ to ‘XVI’ by moving multiple sticks, affecting several characters.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain exactly two horizontal sticks; you cannot remove, add, or alter it, nor use it as a source or destination for a stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Never select the ‘=’ sign as a source or destination in a stick move.
matchstick.example: Removing a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to turn it into ‘‑’, breaking the equality sign.

matchstick.title: Transform numerals via single stick moves
matchstick.principle: Use known one‑stick transformations (e.g., I↔II, V↔X) that keep both characters valid after the move; these are the only safe numeral changes.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a numeral needs to change, consider if a single‑stick transformation exists that yields another valid numeral.
matchstick.example: Attempting to turn X into L by moving a stick, which is not a recognized one‑stick transformation.

matchstick.title: Answer formatting
matchstick.principle: The final output must be a single line starting with ‘Correct version of the equation:’ followed by the equation; missing the prefix or extra lines cause rejection.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After finding a valid equation, output it exactly in the required format as the last line.
matchstick.example: Providing ‘XIII = XII ‑ XII’ without the required prefix.

matchstick.title: Plus-to-minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: If the equation contains a ‘+’, you may move its vertical stick to another character, turning ‘+’ into ‘‑’ while preserving validity of both characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a plus sign is present and converting it to minus could balance the equation, relocate its vertical stick.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from ‘+’ to an ‘I’, leaving ‘‑’ and turning the ‘I’ into ‘II’.

matchstick.title: Within‑character diagonal repositioning
matchstick.principle: You may relocate a diagonal stick within the same numeral (source and destination are the same character), e.g., turning X into V or V into X, without affecting other characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the puzzle involves X or V and a value change of 5 is needed, consider moving a diagonal within the character.
matchstick.example: Moving one diagonal of an X to create a V, reducing its value from 10 to 5.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: You may add a vertical stick to a ‘‑’ to turn it into ‘+’ (or remove a vertical stick from ‘+’ to turn it into ‘‑’), moving exactly one stick from a numeral that can lose a vertical stick (e.g., II or III) to the operator, ensuring both source and destination remain valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a ‘‑’ or ‘+’ and adjusting the operator could help balance the arithmetic, consider moving a vertical stick from a numeral with at least two vertical sticks to the operator (or the reverse).
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick from a numeral II to a ‘‑’ sign, turning the ‘‑’ into ‘+’ and the numeral into I.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model proposes a transformation but does not recompute the numeric values, so it may output a false equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each candidate move, calculate the integer values of both sides and only accept if they match.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving a stick can leave a character with too few or mismatched sticks, producing a shape that is not a recognized Roman numeral.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that both source and destination characters correspond to a valid numeral after the move.

matchstick.why_it_happens: Moving sticks to or from an operator can produce a symbol that is not ‘+’, ‘‑’, or ‘=’, violating the allowed operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure any operator after the move is still a valid ‘+’, ‘‑’, or ‘=’, respecting orientation constraints.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effective removal)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes a stick from a character but does not place it onto another, effectively deleting a stick.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Every stick moved must be placed onto a valid destination character; the move cannot be a deletion.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The final output does not start with the required prefix or is truncated, so the parser cannot extract the answer.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After finding a valid equation, output exactly one line: ‘Correct version of the equation: <equation>’ as the last line, with no extra text.
